boards.school_name: Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College
boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented LSU settings for solo work, group sessions, presentation practice, and outdoor reading, with current access constraints noted.

cards.entity_name: LSU Main Library Collaborative Study Rooms
cards.title: Bring the Group to a Screen-Ready Room
cards.subtitle: Bookable rooms for collaborative work in LSU’s Main Library
cards.notes: Reserve ahead for a two-to-six-person session, then bring a laptop for the room display’s supplied HDMI or USB-C connection.
cards.short_summary: A reservable group workspace with a display, whiteboard, and seating for small teams.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Libraries says these Main Library rooms accommodate groups of two to six; its room guidance identifies displays, whiteboards, and supplied display cables.
cards.access_notes: Available to LSU undergraduate and graduate students. Study spaces close one hour before the library; reservations take priority over walk-up use.

cards.entity_name: LSU Main Library Student Meeting Rooms
cards.title: Practice the Presentation Behind a Door
cards.subtitle: Enclosed Main Library rooms built around a large display and table
cards.notes: Use the enclosed setup to rehearse slides aloud; reserve no more than three hours for the day and return borrowed peripherals afterward.
cards.short_summary: An enclosed option for presentation rehearsal or a focused project meeting.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Libraries describes the Student Meeting Rooms as enclosed rooms with a large display and table, suitable for presentation practice and reservable for up to three hours per day.
cards.access_notes: Available to LSU undergraduate and graduate students. An individual student may reserve one for up to three hours per day; spaces close one hour before the library.

cards.entity_name: LSU Main Library Quiet Study Rooms
cards.title: Keep the Group Session Quiet
cards.subtitle: Reservable rooms for two to six quiet collaborators
cards.notes: Choose this room when the team needs shared space without a loud discussion, and keep the session within the three-hour daily limit.
cards.short_summary: Small-group rooms where collaboration comes with an explicit quiet-use expectation.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Libraries says its Quiet Study Rooms accommodate quiet groups of two to six in the Main Library and may be reserved for up to three hours per day.
cards.access_notes: Available to LSU undergraduate and graduate students. Reservations are limited to three hours per individual student per day; spaces close one hour before the library.

cards.entity_name: LSU Main Library Bookable Study Booths
cards.title: Settle Into a Booth With Power
cards.subtitle: Individual Main Library booths with a desk, lamp, and outlet
cards.notes: Reserve a booth for sustained individual work, use a temporary-storage locker if needed, and never leave books or belongings unattended.
cards.short_summary: A bookable individual station equipped for laptop work and close reading.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Libraries states that every bookable study booth has a desk, reading lamp, and electrical outlet and can be reserved by undergraduate and graduate students.
cards.access_notes: LSU undergraduate and graduate students may reserve a booth daily for up to 14 consecutive days. Ask the Checkout Desk about a lock for temporary storage.

cards.title: Take the Reading Outside in the Quad
cards.subtitle: A central outdoor LSU setting for books, notes, and a laptop
cards.notes: Bring material that works outdoors and pick a comfortable place in the Quad; have an indoor backup ready if weather disrupts the session.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable central-campus alternative to an indoor desk or study room.
cards.evidence_claim: An April 2026 LSU photo feature identifies The Quad as a place where students focus and learn during finals.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: The official feature documents outdoor studying here but does not state hours, reservation rules, or building-style access controls.

cards.entity_name: Hill Memorial Library Quiet Study Room
cards.title: Work Quietly on Hill’s Second Floor
cards.subtitle: A weekday quiet-study room inside Hill Memorial Library
cards.notes: Plan this stop for a weekday between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., finish food or drinks in the lobby, and keep the study room quiet.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet room with defined weekday access and a no-food-or-drink rule.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Libraries says Hill Memorial Library’s second-floor Quiet Study Room is open to students on semester weekdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; food and drink are prohibited there.
cards.access_notes: Open to students during the semester on weekdays, 9 a.m.–5 p.m. Food and drink are prohibited in the room but may be consumed in the first-floor lobby.

cards.entity_name: LSU Student Union Third-Floor Study Pods
cards.title: Plug In at a Divided Study Pod
cards.subtitle: Third-floor Union pods with charging stations and built-in dividers
cards.notes: Head to the Union’s third floor when you need a divided workstation, and bring the charging cable required for your own device.
cards.short_summary: A more separated Union workstation with built-in charging support.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 study-spaces feature documents third-floor Student Union study pods with built-in dividers and charging stations.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: Located on the Student Union’s third floor. The cited feature does not provide operating hours or state whether individual pods can be reserved.

cards.title: Move the Project to the Terrace
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Union seating for solo work or a group project
cards.notes: Use the terrace for work that benefits from fresh air, secure loose papers before opening them, and shift indoors if conditions change.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor study setting suited to either independent work or meeting a project group.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 study-spaces feature says the Student Union Terrace lets students sit outside alone or meet with a group to work on projects.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: Outdoor terrace access may depend on Student Union operations and conditions; the cited source gives no hours or reservation requirements.

cards.title: Find a Work Surface in the BEC Rotunda
cards.subtitle: An indoor Business Education Complex setting with multiple study places
cards.notes: Use the Rotunda for an indoor session between campus commitments, and confirm building access before planning evening or weekend work.
cards.short_summary: A spacious academic-building interior documented by LSU as a place to study.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 study-spaces feature identifies the Business Education Complex Rotunda as offering numerous places for students to study.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: The source documents study use but does not specify public access, room reservations, or current building hours; verify access before going.

cards.title: Study Among the BEC Courtyard Greenery
cards.subtitle: An outdoor Business Education Complex space with benches
cards.notes: Pack a compact study task for a courtyard bench, check the weather first, and keep an indoor alternative ready for heat or rain.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped outdoor option for reading or completing a shorter assignment.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 study-spaces feature documents benches and greenery in the Business Education Complex Courtyard as a setting where students can sit and study.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: The cited source confirms outdoor study seating but does not state hours, reservations, or whether building closures restrict courtyard access.
